# 8. Co-proximity networks

**Module 08 — Co-proximity networks (optional).** Run after module `02`; skip this module if you do not need network analysis. It applies hdWGCNA, translated from genes to marker pairs, to find co-proximity modules: sets of marker pairs whose proximity rises and falls together across the cells of one cell type. It then tests whether each co-proximity module shifts between conditions.

> **Note:** Vocabulary used in this analysis module.
> - A **co-proximity module** is a set of marker pairs found by the network. An **analysis module** is one of the numbered notebooks of this template, such as this one.
> - The **module eigengene** (ME) is one score per cell: the first principal component of the module's marker pairs.
> - **Module membership** (hdWGCNA's **kME**) is a marker pair's correlation with its module's eigengene: how closely the pair follows the module.
> - The **hub pairs** are the marker pairs with the highest module membership in their module.
> - A **network** is fit per stratum (for example a cancer type), cell type and network cell set (for example one condition). It is named `stratum · cell type · network` (the stratum only with a `stratify_column`), and its modules M1, M2, ... are numbered within it, so M1 of one network is unrelated to M1 of another.

> **Note:** The network sweep takes a few minutes. Module preservation (section 8.5) is opt-in and can take hours.

```{r}
#| label: module08_setup

here::i_am("modules/08_coproximity_networks.qmd")

source(here::here("modules", "common_setup.R"))

if (!exists("pg_data", inherits = TRUE)) {
  pg_data <- load_checkpoint("annotated_seurat_object.rds")
}
if (!exists("markers_to_test", inherits = TRUE)) {
  markers_to_test <- load_checkpoint("markers_to_test.rds")
}

# hdWGCNA is called as hdWGCNA:: and never attached: library(hdWGCNA)
# attaches matrixStats, which masks dplyr::count.
if (!requireNamespace("hdWGCNA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop(
    "Module 08 needs the hdWGCNA package. Install it with ",
    "pak::pak(\"smorabit/hdWGCNA@v0.4.12\")."
  )
}

module08_dir <- here::here("results/08_coproximity_networks")
dir.create(module08_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 8.0. Set parameters

> **Decision checkpoint** (contrast, strata, cell types and network cells)  
> Set `reference_condition` to the same value as in module `05`. Choose a `stratify_column` to fit separate networks per stratum (for example per cancer type), narrow `coproximity_cell_types` to the cell types you care about, and choose which cells the networks are built on with `network_cells`.

Every other level of `contrast_column` becomes a target condition and is compared to the reference condition.

`network_cells` sets which cells each network is built on:

- `"reference"` (default): only the reference condition's cells. Co-proximity modules that exist only in a target condition are invisible. Module `05`'s differential colocalization covers gained proximity.
- `"each"`: one network per condition, so each condition gets its own modules. The differential module eigengene test (8.3) is then run for the modules of every network; for the networks of a target condition it is mildly circular, because their modules were fit on the cells the test compares.
- `"all"`: one network on the cells of every condition. The test is mildly circular for every module, the larger condition dominates the network, and module preservation (8.5) is skipped.

`stratify_column` names a column whose values each get their own networks, for example a cancer type or tissue, so that modules are not driven by differences between strata. Leave it `NULL` to fit one set of networks on all cells.

`donor_column` names the column that pairs samples across conditions, such as a donor or patient column of `metadata.csv`. With it, 8.3 reports how many donors shift each module in the same direction as the test. Leave it `NULL` for unpaired designs.

`marker_labels_path` points to a table with one row per marker (column `marker`) and a category per marker in `marker_label_column`. The module graphs (8.4) fill each marker with its category and count the markers per category. The template ships `modules/reference/marker_labels.csv` for the Proxiome Immuno 155 panel (`proxiome-v2-immuno-155-v2.0`, 155 markers and 3 isotype controls). Its `immune_process` column (the default) groups the markers into 12 curated immune processes; other columns are `family` (19 molecular families), `expression_context` (the cell lineages that express the marker) and `signal_polarity`. Set `marker_labels_path` to `NULL` to draw all markers alike.

Each network's fit is cached under `networks/`. Set `rebuild_networks <- TRUE` after changing any setting in 8.0, 8.1 or 8.5, or the old fits and preservation results are reused. There are no cache keys: the cache does not notice changed settings.

`markers_to_test` comes from module `02`. To use other markers, override it before this section.

This analysis module writes the following files:

```
results/08_coproximity_networks/
├── sweep_summary.csv
├── dme_results.csv
├── dme_results.rds
├── dme_summary_dotplot.{png,pdf}
├── preservation_results.csv                    # opt-in
├── networks/                                   # cache; delete or set rebuild_networks to refresh
│   ├── {stratum}_{cell_type}_{network}.rds
│   └── {stratum}_{cell_type}_{network}_preservation.rds   # opt-in
└── {stratum}/{cell_type}/{network}_network/     # one folder per network; no {stratum}/ level without stratify_column
    ├── soft_powers.{png,pdf}
    ├── dendrogram.{png,pdf}
    ├── modules.csv
    ├── hub_pairs.csv
    ├── kme.{png,pdf}
    ├── me_umap.{png,pdf}
    ├── me_violins.{png,pdf}
    ├── dme_lollipop.{png,pdf}
    ├── preservation_zsummary.{png,pdf}         # opt-in
    └── module_graphs/
        └── M1.{png,pdf}, M2.{png,pdf}, ...
```

Folder and file names replace characters other than letters and digits with `_`. Without a `stratify_column`, the stratum is left out of the network names, folders and cache files.

The HTML report shows the sweep summary, the significant differential module eigengene rows and the summary dotplot. Per-network figures are written to files only.

```{r}
#| label: module08_parameters

contrast_column <- "condition"
reference_condition <- "donor1" # keep consistent with module 05
# Column whose values each get their own networks; NULL fits one set of
# networks on all cells.
stratify_column <- NULL
# Column that pairs samples across conditions; NULL skips donor agreement.
donor_column <- NULL
# Narrow to the cell types you care about.
coproximity_cell_types <- sort(unique(pg_data$cell_annotation))
network_cells <- "reference" # "reference", "each" or "all"
rebuild_networks <- FALSE
# One category per marker for the module graphs; NULL draws all markers alike.
marker_labels_path <- here::here("modules", "reference", "marker_labels.csv")
marker_label_column <- "immune_process"

contrast_values <- pg_data[[contrast_column, drop = TRUE]]
if (!reference_condition %in% contrast_values) {
  stop(
    "reference_condition '", reference_condition, "' is not a value of ",
    "pg_data$", contrast_column, "."
  )
}
if (!network_cells %in% c("reference", "each", "all")) {
  stop("network_cells must be \"reference\", \"each\" or \"all\".")
}

target_conditions <- setdiff(unique(contrast_values), reference_condition)
all_conditions <- c(reference_condition, target_conditions)
# Named list: one entry per network fit within a stratum and cell type; the
# name is the network's name and the value the conditions it is built on.
network_sets <- switch(
  network_cells,
  reference = set_names(list(reference_condition), reference_condition),
  each = set_names(as.list(all_conditions), all_conditions),
  all = list(all = all_conditions)
)
stratum_values <- if (is.null(stratify_column)) {
  rep("all cells", ncol(pg_data))
} else {
  pg_data[[stratify_column, drop = TRUE]]
}
strata <- sort(unique(stratum_values))
# Network names and folders include the stratum only with a stratify_column.
use_stratum_names <- !is.null(stratify_column)
```

## 8.1. Build co-proximity networks

For each stratum, cell type and network cell set, the network is built in the steps of the hdWGCNA single-cell vignette, with marker pairs in the place of genes:

1. **Marker pairs.** The proximity scores (`log2_ratio`) of the stratum's cells of the cell type become a pairs × cells matrix. Pairs whose two markers are both in `markers_to_test` and that are detected in at least `min_pair_detection` of the cells of all the stratum's network cell sets are kept, so the networks of one stratum and cell type share their pairs.
2. **Metacells.** Neighbouring cells of the same condition and sample are averaged into metacells (`metacell_k` cells each) to reduce the sparsity of single-cell proximity scores.
3. **Soft power.** Correlations between pairs are raised to a power so that the network approximates a scale-free topology. By default the lowest power above 3 that reaches a scale-free fit R² ≥ 0.8 is picked per network.
4. **Network.** A signed network is built from biweight midcorrelations (bicor) on the metacells of the network's conditions, and its topological overlap is clustered into a dendrogram.
5. **Modules.** The dendrogram is cut into co-proximity modules of at least `min_module_size` pairs, and similar modules are merged (`merge_cut_height`). Pairs that fit no module go to the grey module, which is left out of every readout. Modules are named M1, M2, ... per network.

> **Decision checkpoint** (network settings)  
> Set the pair, metacell and module floors. Networks that fall below a floor are skipped and listed with the reason in `sweep_summary.csv`. Leave `soft_power <- NULL` to pick the power per network, or set a number to use it for every network.

```{r}
#| label: module08_network_settings

min_pair_detection <- 0.10
min_network_pairs <- 100
metacell_k <- 25
metacell_min_cells <- 50
min_network_metacells <- 20
soft_power <- NULL # NULL = auto per network; a number applies to all
min_module_size <- 30
merge_cut_height <- 0.2
```

> **Note:** Proximity scores are zero-filled: a zero means both "pair not detected" and "no deviation from the expected proximity". The detection floor counts non-zero scores.

> **Note:** Metacells average cells of similar abundance, not similar proximity, because the neighbours are found on the abundance-based `harmony` reduction. The vignette notes that a `metacell_k` of 20-75 usually works.

> **Note:** A sample needs at least `metacell_min_cells` cells of the cell type to contribute metacells, and a network needs `min_network_metacells` metacells. If a cell type falls short, merge small annotations or lower `metacell_k`, but not below about 15.

> **Note:** hdWGCNA warns that fewer than 500 features were selected; this is expected for PNA, which has a few thousand marker pairs. bicor falls back to Pearson correlation for pairs with zero median absolute deviation.

> **Note:** hdWGCNA 0.4.12 does not run as shipped with SeuratObject 5.3.0. `common_setup.R` lets `GetAssayData()` and `SetAssayData()` accept hdWGCNA's `slot =` again, and the metacells of all samples, which hdWGCNA merges into one layer per sample, are joined into one layer below.

```{r}
#| label: module08_build_networks

networks_dir <- file.path(module08_dir, "networks")
dir.create(networks_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

coproximity_fits <- list()
fit_index <- tibble()
sweep_summary <- tibble()

for (stratum in strata) {
  for (cell_type in coproximity_cell_types) {
    # Name parts of this stratum and cell type's networks: fit_id, folders
    # and cache files leave the stratum out without a stratify_column.
    name_parts <- c(if (use_stratum_names) stratum, cell_type)
    stratum_slug <- str_replace_all(paste(name_parts, collapse = " "), "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_")
    stratum_cells <- colnames(pg_data)[
      stratum_values == stratum & pg_data$cell_annotation == cell_type
    ]
    stratum_conditions <- contrast_values[stratum_values == stratum & pg_data$cell_annotation == cell_type]
    cache_paths <- file.path(
      networks_dir,
      paste0(stratum_slug, "_", str_replace_all(names(network_sets), "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_"), ".rds")
    )

    if (all(file.exists(cache_paths)) && !rebuild_networks) {
      for (network_name in names(network_sets)) {
        network_fit <- readRDS(cache_paths[names(network_sets) == network_name])
        fit_id <- paste(c(name_parts, paste(network_name, "network")), collapse = " · ")
        coproximity_fits[[fit_id]] <- network_fit
        fit_index <- bind_rows(fit_index, network_fit@misc$coproximity_index)
        sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, network_fit@misc$coproximity_summary)
      }
      next
    }

    summary_template <- tibble(
      stratum = stratum,
      cell_type = cell_type,
      network = names(network_sets),
      n_cells_network = NA_integer_,
      n_pairs = NA_integer_,
      n_network_metacells = NA_integer_,
      n_network_samples = NA_integer_,
      soft_power = NA_real_,
      power_fallback = NA,
      n_modules = NA_integer_,
      status = "ok"
    )

    if (is.null(markers_to_test[[cell_type]]) || length(stratum_cells) == 0) {
      summary_template$status <- "no cells or not in markers_to_test"
      warning(paste(name_parts, collapse = " / "), ": ", summary_template$status[1], "; skipped")
      sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, summary_template)
      next
    }

    # Pairs x cells, data layer only, zero-filled.
    stratum_object <-
      subset(pg_data, cells = stratum_cells) |>
      ProximityScoresToAssay(
        assay = "PNA",
        new_assay = "proximity",
        values_from = "log2_ratio",
        lazy = TRUE
      )
    DefaultAssay(stratum_object) <- "proximity"

    # One pair set per stratum and cell type, detected over the cells of all
    # its network cell sets, so all its networks share their pairs.
    proximity_matrix <- LayerData(stratum_object, layer = "data")
    pair_markers <- str_split_fixed(rownames(proximity_matrix), ":", 2)
    is_network_cell <- stratum_object[[contrast_column, drop = TRUE]] %in% unlist(network_sets)
    pair_detection <- rowMeans(proximity_matrix[, is_network_cell] != 0)
    network_pairs <- rownames(proximity_matrix)[
      pair_markers[, 1] %in% markers_to_test[[cell_type]] &
        pair_markers[, 2] %in% markers_to_test[[cell_type]] &
        pair_detection >= min_pair_detection
    ]
    summary_template$n_pairs <- length(network_pairs)
    if (length(network_pairs) < min_network_pairs) {
      summary_template$status <- paste("fewer than", min_network_pairs, "pairs")
      warning(paste(name_parts, collapse = " / "), ": ", summary_template$status[1], "; skipped")
      sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, summary_template)
      next
    }

    stratum_object <- hdWGCNA::SetupForWGCNA(
      stratum_object,
      features = network_pairs,
      wgcna_name = stratum_slug
    )
    # Metacells are built for every condition; 8.3 and 8.5 use all of them.
    metacell_result <- tryCatch(
      hdWGCNA::MetacellsByGroups(
        stratum_object,
        group.by = c(contrast_column, "sample_alias"),
        ident.group = contrast_column,
        reduction = "harmony",
        dims = 1:20,
        k = metacell_k,
        max_shared = round(0.6 * metacell_k),
        min_cells = metacell_min_cells,
        assay = "proximity",
        slot = "data",
        layer = "data",
        mode = "average",
        verbose = FALSE
      ),
      error = conditionMessage
    )
    if (is.character(metacell_result)) {
      summary_template$status <- paste("metacells failed:", metacell_result)
      warning(paste(name_parts, collapse = " / "), ": ", summary_template$status[1], "; skipped")
      sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, summary_template)
      next
    }
    # MetacellsByGroups merges the per-group metacell objects into one layer
    # per group (counts.1, counts.2, ...); SetDatExpr needs a single layer.
    stratum_object <- hdWGCNA::SetMetacellObject(
      metacell_result,
      JoinLayers(hdWGCNA::GetMetacellObject(metacell_result)),
      wgcna_name = stratum_slug
    )
    metacell_meta <- hdWGCNA::GetMetacellObject(stratum_object)[[]]

    for (network_name in names(network_sets)) {
      summary_row <- filter(summary_template, network == network_name)
      summary_row$n_cells_network <- sum(stratum_conditions %in% network_sets[[network_name]])
      fit_id <- paste(c(name_parts, paste(network_name, "network")), collapse = " · ")
      fit_dir <- do.call(file.path, as.list(c(
        module08_dir,
        str_replace_all(name_parts, "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_"),
        paste0(str_replace_all(network_name, "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_"), "_network")
      )))
      cache_path <- cache_paths[names(network_sets) == network_name]

      # A network condition without metacells is left out of the network;
      # the network is skipped only if none of its conditions has metacells.
      network_groups <- intersect(network_sets[[network_name]], metacell_meta[[contrast_column]])
      if (length(network_groups) == 0) {
        summary_row$status <- "network conditions below metacell_min_cells"
        warning(fit_id, ": ", summary_row$status, "; skipped")
        sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, summary_row)
        next
      }

      # mode = "average" puts the averaged log2_ratio in the metacell counts
      # layer. It is already on the log2_ratio scale, so it is read from
      # counts and NormalizeMetacells is never called.
      network_fit <- hdWGCNA::SetDatExpr(
        stratum_object,
        group_name = network_groups,
        group.by = contrast_column,
        assay = "proximity",
        slot = "counts",
        layer = "counts"
      )
      summary_row$n_network_metacells <- nrow(hdWGCNA::GetDatExpr(network_fit))
      summary_row$n_network_samples <- n_distinct(
        metacell_meta$sample_alias[metacell_meta[[contrast_column]] %in% network_groups]
      )
      if (summary_row$n_network_metacells < min_network_metacells) {
        summary_row$status <- paste("fewer than", min_network_metacells, "network metacells")
        warning(fit_id, ": ", summary_row$status, "; skipped")
        sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, summary_row)
        next
      }
      if (summary_row$n_network_samples == 1) {
        warning(fit_id, ": network metacells come from a single sample; modules may be sample-specific")
      }

      # The summary_row assignments inside tryCatch() land in the loop's scope.
      network_result <- tryCatch(
        {
          network_fit <- hdWGCNA::TestSoftPowers(
            network_fit,
            networkType = "signed",
            corFnc = "bicor"
          )
          power_table <- hdWGCNA::GetPowerTable(network_fit)
          auto_powers <- power_table$Power[
            power_table$Power > 3 & power_table$SFT.R.sq >= 0.8
          ]
          summary_row$power_fallback <- is.null(soft_power) && length(auto_powers) == 0
          summary_row$soft_power <- soft_power %||% min(auto_powers, Inf)
          if (summary_row$power_fallback) {
            # WGCNA FAQ powers for signed networks, by number of samples
            # (metacells).
            summary_row$soft_power <- case_when(
              summary_row$n_network_metacells < 30 ~ 16,
              summary_row$n_network_metacells < 40 ~ 14,
              .default = 12
            )
            warning(
              fit_id, ": no soft power reached scale-free R^2 >= 0.8; ",
              "using fallback power ", summary_row$soft_power
            )
          }

          network_fit <- hdWGCNA::ConstructNetwork(
            network_fit,
            soft_power = summary_row$soft_power,
            networkType = "signed",
            TOMType = "signed",
            corType = "bicor",
            minModuleSize = min_module_size,
            mergeCutHeight = merge_cut_height,
            tom_outdir = tempdir(),
            tom_name = paste0(stratum_slug, "_", make.names(network_name)),
            overwrite_tom = TRUE,
            setDatExpr = FALSE,
            verbose = 0
          )

          # Plain MEs on all of the stratum's cells; kME on the network cells.
          network_fit |>
            hdWGCNA::ModuleEigengenes(
              group.by.vars = NULL,
              assay = "proximity",
              verbose = FALSE
            ) |>
            hdWGCNA::ModuleConnectivity(
              group.by = contrast_column,
              group_name = network_groups,
              harmonized = FALSE,
              assay = "proximity",
              layer = "data"
            ) |>
            hdWGCNA::ResetModuleNames(new_name = "M")
        },
        error = conditionMessage
      )
      if (is.character(network_result)) {
        summary_row$status <- paste("network failed:", network_result)
        warning(fit_id, ": ", summary_row$status, "; skipped")
        sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, summary_row)
        next
      }
      network_fit <- network_result
      modules <- hdWGCNA::GetModules(network_fit)
      summary_row$n_modules <- n_distinct(modules$module[modules$module != "grey"])
      if (summary_row$n_modules == 0) {
        summary_row$status <- "no co-proximity modules"
        warning(fit_id, ": ", summary_row$status, "; skipped")
        sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, summary_row)
        next
      }

      # DietSeurat keeps @misc (misc = TRUE), where hdWGCNA stores the fit. The
      # summary and index rows are stored with it, so a cached fit restores
      # them.
      index_row <- tibble(
        fit_id = fit_id,
        stratum = stratum,
        cell_type = cell_type,
        network = network_name,
        fit_dir = fit_dir
      )
      network_fit <- DietSeurat(
        network_fit,
        assays = "proximity",
        dimreducs = c("harmony", "harmony_umap")
      )
      network_fit@misc$coproximity_summary <- summary_row
      network_fit@misc$coproximity_index <- index_row
      saveRDS(network_fit, cache_path)
      coproximity_fits[[fit_id]] <- network_fit
      fit_index <- bind_rows(fit_index, index_row)
      sweep_summary <- bind_rows(sweep_summary, summary_row)

      dir.create(fit_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
      export_plot(
        filename = file.path(fit_dir, "soft_powers"),
        plot = patchwork::wrap_plots(hdWGCNA::PlotSoftPowers(network_fit), ncol = 2),
        width = 10,
        height = 7
      )
      # PlotDendrogram draws with base graphics, so it is saved per device.
      png(file.path(fit_dir, "dendrogram.png"), width = 8, height = 4, units = "in", res = 300)
      hdWGCNA::PlotDendrogram(network_fit, main = fit_id)
      dev.off()
      pdf(file.path(fit_dir, "dendrogram.pdf"), width = 8, height = 4)
      hdWGCNA::PlotDendrogram(network_fit, main = fit_id)
      dev.off()
    }
  }
}

write.csv(sweep_summary, file.path(module08_dir, "sweep_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
sweep_summary
```

## 8.2. Module composition

Each co-proximity module is described by its marker pairs and their module membership (kME), the correlation of a pair's proximity score with the module eigengene. A pair with a high membership follows the module closely, and the pairs with the highest membership are the module's hub pairs: they are the best single summary of what the module captures. Membership is computed on the network's own cells.

For each network, this section writes:

- `modules.csv`: one row per marker pair in a co-proximity module, with its module, its kME in that module and its mean `log2_ratio` per condition (over the stratum's single cells of the cell type, zeros included).
- `hub_pairs.csv`: the 10 pairs with the highest kME per module.
- `kme`: each module's pairs ranked by kME, with the hub pairs named.
- `me_umap`: the module eigengene of each cell on the `harmony_umap` embedding, one panel per module.

```{r}
#| label: module08_module_composition

if (length(coproximity_fits) == 0) {
  message("No network was fitted (see sweep_summary.csv); 8.2 is skipped.")
}

for (fit_id in names(coproximity_fits)) {
  network_fit <- coproximity_fits[[fit_id]]
  fit_dir <- filter(fit_index, fit_id == .env$fit_id)$fit_dir
  cell_conditions <- network_fit[[contrast_column, drop = TRUE]]
  proximity_matrix <- LayerData(network_fit, layer = "data")

  # Keep each pair's kME in its own module only; grey is dropped.
  module_membership <-
    hdWGCNA::GetModules(network_fit) |>
    filter(module != "grey") |>
    mutate(module = as.character(module)) |>
    pivot_longer(
      starts_with("kME_"),
      names_to = "kme_module",
      names_prefix = "kME_",
      values_to = "kME"
    ) |>
    filter(kme_module == module) |>
    separate_wider_delim(
      gene_name,
      delim = ":",
      names = c("marker_1", "marker_2"),
      cols_remove = FALSE
    )
  for (condition in all_conditions) {
    module_membership[[paste0("mean_log2_ratio_", condition)]] <- rowMeans(
      proximity_matrix[
        module_membership$gene_name,
        cell_conditions == condition,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    )
  }
  module_membership <-
    module_membership |>
    select(marker_1, marker_2, module, kME, starts_with("mean_log2_ratio_")) |>
    arrange(str_rank(module, numeric = TRUE), desc(kME))
  write.csv(module_membership, file.path(fit_dir, "modules.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  # 10 hub pairs per module, as in the hdWGCNA vignette.
  write.csv(
    slice_max(module_membership, kME, n = 10, by = module, with_ties = FALSE),
    file.path(fit_dir, "hub_pairs.csv"),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  n_modules <- n_distinct(module_membership$module)
  n_panel_columns <- min(4, n_modules)
  n_panel_rows <- ceiling(n_modules / n_panel_columns)
  export_plot(
    filename = file.path(fit_dir, "kme"),
    plot = hdWGCNA::PlotKMEs(network_fit, ncol = n_panel_columns),
    width = 4 * n_panel_columns,
    height = 3 * n_panel_rows
  )
  # features = "MEs": the plain eigengenes, as everywhere in this module.
  export_plot(
    filename = file.path(fit_dir, "me_umap"),
    plot = patchwork::wrap_plots(
      hdWGCNA::ModuleFeaturePlot(network_fit, reduction = "harmony_umap", features = "MEs"),
      ncol = n_panel_columns
    ),
    width = 3 * n_panel_columns,
    height = 3 * n_panel_rows
  )
}
```

## 8.3. Differential module eigengenes

A differential module eigengene (DME) test asks whether a co-proximity module as a whole shifts between conditions. For each network, co-proximity module and target condition, the module eigengenes of the target cells are compared to those of the reference cells of the same stratum and cell type with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test. The effect size is `diff_median`, the median eigengene of the target cells minus that of the reference cells. A positive `diff_median` means the module's marker pairs are, together, more colocalized in the target condition, and a negative one means less, for pairs with a positive kME.

A comparison is skipped when either condition has fewer than 10 cells. P-values are adjusted with Benjamini-Hochberg across all networks, target conditions and modules, as in module `05`. With a `donor_column`, each donor's shift is the median eigengene of its target sample minus that of its reference sample; `n_donors_same_direction` counts the donors whose shift has the sign of `diff_median`. Rows with `p_adj < 0.05` are printed below; all rows are written to `dme_results.csv` and `dme_results.rds`.

> **Note:** Cells are treated as independent observations, although cells of one sample are not (pseudo-replication). The p-values therefore overstate the confidence, and with thousands of cells even small shifts become significant. Read `diff_median` together with the donor agreement and the `me_violins` plots, where each point is the median of one sample.

> **Note:** With one sample per condition, condition cannot be separated from sample: a significant module may reflect a difference between the two samples rather than between the conditions. The test still runs, and a warning is emitted.

> **Note:** For networks built on a target condition, or on all conditions, the modules were fit on cells the test compares, so the test is mildly circular (see 8.0).

```{r}
#| label: module08_differential_module_eigengenes

if (length(coproximity_fits) == 0) {
  message("No network was fitted (see sweep_summary.csv); 8.3 is skipped.")
}

dme_results <- tibble()

# condition_palette is named by metadata$condition (common_setup.R); use it
# only if it covers the contrast levels, else ggplot's default colours.
violin_fill_scale <- if (all(all_conditions %in% names(condition_palette))) {
  scale_fill_manual(values = condition_palette)
}

for (fit_id in names(coproximity_fits)) {
  network_fit <- coproximity_fits[[fit_id]]
  fit_row <- filter(fit_index, fit_id == .env$fit_id)
  cell_conditions <- network_fit[[contrast_column, drop = TRUE]]

  # Plain eigengenes, one row per cell and module, grey dropped.
  module_eigengenes <-
    hdWGCNA::GetMEs(network_fit, harmonized = FALSE) |>
    select(-any_of("grey")) |>
    mutate(
      condition = cell_conditions,
      sample = network_fit$sample_alias,
      donor = if (is.null(donor_column)) NA_character_ else network_fit[[donor_column, drop = TRUE]]
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(-c(condition, sample, donor), names_to = "module", values_to = "eigengene") |>
    mutate(
      condition = factor(condition, levels = all_conditions),
      module = factor(module, levels = str_sort(unique(module), numeric = TRUE))
    )

  sample_medians <- summarise(
    module_eigengenes,
    eigengene = median(eigengene),
    .by = c(module, condition, sample, donor)
  )
  n_modules <- nlevels(module_eigengenes$module)
  n_panel_columns <- min(4, n_modules)
  n_panel_rows <- ceiling(n_modules / n_panel_columns)
  export_plot(
    filename = file.path(fit_row$fit_dir, "me_violins"),
    plot = module_eigengenes |>
      ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = eigengene, fill = condition)) +
      geom_violin(scale = "width") +
      geom_point(data = sample_medians, size = 2, show.legend = FALSE) +
      facet_wrap(~module, scales = "free_y", ncol = n_panel_columns) +
      violin_fill_scale +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Module eigengenes:", fit_id),
        subtitle = "Points: per-sample medians",
        x = NULL,
        y = "Module eigengene",
        fill = contrast_column
      ),
    width = 3 * n_panel_columns + 1,
    height = 3 * n_panel_rows
  )

  # At least 10 cells per condition, as pixelatorR's min_cells_per_group.
  cell_counts <- table(factor(cell_conditions, levels = all_conditions))
  comparable_targets <- target_conditions[
    cell_counts[target_conditions] >= 10 & cell_counts[[reference_condition]] >= 10
  ]
  if (length(comparable_targets) == 0) {
    message(fit_id, ": no target condition with at least 10 cells next to at least 10 reference cells; DME skipped")
    next
  }
  samples_per_condition <- tapply(network_fit$sample_alias, cell_conditions, n_distinct)[
    c(reference_condition, comparable_targets)
  ]
  if (any(samples_per_condition == 1)) {
    warning(fit_id, ": a compared condition has a single sample, so condition cannot be separated from sample")
  }

  # FindDMEs is not used: it clips negative eigengenes to 0 before testing,
  # which discards the lower half of a signed proximity eigengene.
  for (target in comparable_targets) {
    target_results <-
      module_eigengenes |>
      summarise(
        n_cells_reference = sum(condition == reference_condition),
        n_cells_target = sum(condition == target),
        median_reference = median(eigengene[condition == reference_condition]),
        median_target = median(eigengene[condition == target]),
        p_value = wilcox.test(
          eigengene[condition == target],
          eigengene[condition == reference_condition]
        )$p.value,
        .by = module
      ) |>
      mutate(diff_median = median_target - median_reference)

    donor_agreement <-
      sample_medians |>
      filter(condition %in% c(reference_condition, target), !is.na(donor)) |>
      select(module, donor, condition, eigengene) |>
      # names_expand keeps a column per condition when no donor is left
      # (no donor_column, or no donor with both samples).
      pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = eigengene, names_expand = TRUE) |>
      filter(!is.na(.data[[reference_condition]]), !is.na(.data[[target]])) |>
      mutate(donor_shift = .data[[target]] - .data[[reference_condition]]) |>
      left_join(select(target_results, module, diff_median), by = "module") |>
      summarise(
        n_donors = n(),
        n_donors_same_direction = sum(sign(donor_shift) == sign(diff_median)),
        .by = module
      )

    dme_results <- bind_rows(
      dme_results,
      target_results |>
        left_join(donor_agreement, by = "module") |>
        mutate(
          fit_id = fit_id,
          stratum = fit_row$stratum,
          cell_type = fit_row$cell_type,
          network = fit_row$network,
          target = target,
          reference = reference_condition,
          module = as.character(module)
        )
    )
  }
}

if (nrow(dme_results) > 0) {
  dme_results <-
    dme_results |>
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) |>
    relocate(fit_id, stratum, cell_type, network, module, target, reference) |>
    arrange(stratum, cell_type, network, target, str_rank(module, numeric = TRUE))
}
write.csv(dme_results, file.path(module08_dir, "dme_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(dme_results, file.path(module08_dir, "dme_results.rds"))

if (nrow(dme_results) == 0 || !any(dme_results$p_adj < 0.05)) {
  message("No significant modules (p_adj < 0.05).")
} else {
  filter(dme_results, p_adj < 0.05) |>
    select(stratum, cell_type, network, module, target, diff_median, p_adj, any_of(c("n_donors_same_direction", "n_donors"))) |>
    print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
}
```

The summary dotplot shows every tested module at once: one row per cell type, one column per module, one panel per stratum (rows) and network (columns). Colour is `diff_median`, size is −log10 `p_adj` (capped at 20), and modules with `p_adj ≥ 0.05` are faded. Module numbers are local to a network, so a column does not link modules across panels.

```{r}
#| label: module08_dme_summary_dotplot

if (nrow(dme_results) == 0) {
  message("No module was tested; the DME dotplots are skipped.")
} else {
  dme_plot_data <-
    dme_results |>
    mutate(
      module = factor(module, levels = str_sort(unique(module), numeric = TRUE)),
      network = factor(paste(network, "network"), levels = paste(names(network_sets), "network")),
      significant = p_adj < 0.05,
      neg_log10_p_adj = pmin(-log10(pmax(p_adj, min_p_value_threshold)), 20)
    )
  shift_limits <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(dme_plot_data$diff_median))

  dme_summary_dotplot <-
    ggplot(dme_plot_data, aes(module, cell_type)) +
    geom_point(
      aes(fill = diff_median, size = neg_log10_p_adj, alpha = significant),
      shape = 21,
      colour = "grey30"
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = gradient_palette,
      limits = shift_limits,
      name = paste0("Module shift\ntarget − ", reference_condition, "\n(median ME)")
    ) +
    scale_size(range = c(2, 9), name = "−log10 adj. p", breaks = c(5, 10, 20), labels = c("5", "10", "≥20")) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.3, `TRUE` = 1), guide = "none") +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(stratum), cols = vars(network, target), labeller = label_value) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Differential module eigengenes vs", reference_condition),
      x = "Module",
      y = NULL
    )

  # PNG through export_plot; the PDF through cairo_pdf, because the default
  # pdf() device cannot encode the minus sign of the legends.
  export_plot(
    filename = file.path(module08_dir, "dme_summary_dotplot"),
    plot = dme_summary_dotplot,
    width = 4 + 0.45 * nlevels(dme_plot_data$module) * n_distinct(dme_plot_data$network) * n_distinct(dme_plot_data$target),
    height = 2 + 3 * n_distinct(dme_plot_data$stratum),
    file_formats = "png"
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(module08_dir, "dme_summary_dotplot.pdf"),
    plot = dme_summary_dotplot,
    width = 4 + 0.45 * nlevels(dme_plot_data$module) * n_distinct(dme_plot_data$network) * n_distinct(dme_plot_data$target),
    height = 2 + 3 * n_distinct(dme_plot_data$stratum),
    device = cairo_pdf
  )
  dme_summary_dotplot
}
```

Each network also gets a lollipop plot, `dme_lollipop`, with one row per module, sorted by `diff_median`. Points are filled by `diff_median` and faded when `p_adj ≥ 0.05`. All lollipop plots share the x axis and the colour scale, so their shifts can be compared.

```{r}
#| label: module08_dme_lollipops

if (nrow(dme_results) > 0) {
  shift_x_limits <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(dme_plot_data$diff_median)) * 1.05
  for (fit_id in unique(dme_plot_data$fit_id)) {
    fit_dme <-
      dme_plot_data |>
      filter(fit_id == .env$fit_id) |>
      mutate(module = fct_reorder(as.character(module), diff_median))
    dme_lollipop <-
      ggplot(fit_dme, aes(diff_median, module)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
      geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = diff_median, yend = module), colour = "grey60", linewidth = 1) +
      geom_point(aes(fill = diff_median, alpha = significant), shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "grey20") +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = shift_x_limits) +
      scale_fill_gradientn(colours = gradient_palette, limits = shift_limits, guide = "none") +
      scale_alpha_manual(
        values = c(`FALSE` = 0.3, `TRUE` = 1),
        labels = c(`FALSE` = "not significant", `TRUE` = "adj. p < 0.05"),
        name = NULL,
        drop = FALSE
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") +
      labs(
        title = fit_id,
        x = paste0("Module shift, ", paste(unique(fit_dme$target), collapse = ", "), " − ", reference_condition, " (median ME)"),
        y = "Module"
      )
    if (n_distinct(fit_dme$target) > 1) {
      dme_lollipop <- dme_lollipop + facet_wrap(~target)
    }

    fit_dir <- filter(fit_index, fit_id == .env$fit_id)$fit_dir
    lollipop_height <- 1.6 + 0.32 * n_distinct(fit_dme$module)
    export_plot(
      filename = file.path(fit_dir, "dme_lollipop"),
      plot = dme_lollipop,
      width = 6 * n_distinct(fit_dme$target),
      height = lollipop_height,
      file_formats = "png"
    )
    ggsave(
      file.path(fit_dir, "dme_lollipop.pdf"),
      plot = dme_lollipop,
      width = 6 * n_distinct(fit_dme$target),
      height = lollipop_height,
      device = cairo_pdf
    )
  }
}
```

## 8.4. Module graphs

A module graph is this analysis module's own figure, not an hdWGCNA plot. It draws one co-proximity module as a network: the nodes are markers and each edge is one of the module's marker pairs. For each network, co-proximity module and target condition with a DME test, it is written to `{network folder}/module_graphs/{module}` (with `_{target}` appended when there are several target conditions).

How to read it:

- **Edges.** All the module's pairs in its largest connected component are drawn; self-pairs (A:A) are not. The caption gives how many of the module's pairs are drawn.
- **Edge colour** is Δ proximity: the pair's mean `log2_ratio` in the target condition minus that in the reference condition, over single cells, with cells where the pair is not detected counted as 0. The mean is used, not the median, because most pairs are undetected in many cells: their median is then 0 and hides a change in how many cells colocalize the pair. Module `05`'s differential colocalization reports the median difference (`diff_median`) with a test per pair; use module `05` for per-pair significance. Red means more colocalized in the target condition, blue less.
- **Edge width and opacity** show module membership (kME): thick, opaque edges are the pairs that follow the module most closely.
- **Hub pairs.** The three pairs with the highest membership have a thin black outline, and their markers are drawn as large nodes with bold, dark-orange labels. They are listed in the caption.
- **Labels** are drawn only for the markers of the module's 10 pairs with the highest membership; the other markers are small points.
- **Fill.** Nodes and labels are filled by the marker's category (`marker_label_column`), and the panel on the right counts the drawn markers per category.
- **Title** gives the module's DME result (`diff_median`, `p_adj` and, with a `donor_column`, the donor agreement).

```{r}
#| label: module08_module_graph_settings

n_label_pairs <- 10
n_hub_pairs <- 3
hub_label_colour <- "#C2560A"

# One fixed fill per category, shared by every graph. Only the categories of
# the markers in markers_to_test are coloured; with 12 or fewer, Set3 is
# used, with its grey (9th) colour, which reads as "missing", replaced.
marker_categories <- if (is.null(marker_labels_path)) {
  tibble(marker = unique(unlist(markers_to_test)), category = "marker")
} else {
  read.csv(marker_labels_path) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(marker, category = .data[[marker_label_column]])
}
category_levels <- sort(unique(
  marker_categories$category[marker_categories$marker %in% unlist(markers_to_test)]
))
set3_colours <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Set3")
set3_colours[9] <- "#E5C494"
category_palette <- set_names(
  if (length(category_levels) <= 12) {
    set3_colours[seq_along(category_levels)]
  } else {
    colorRampPalette(set3_colours)(length(category_levels))
  },
  category_levels
)
```

```{r}
#| label: module08_module_graphs

for (fit_id in unique(dme_results$fit_id)) {
  fit_dir <- filter(fit_index, fit_id == .env$fit_id)$fit_dir
  module_graphs_dir <- file.path(fit_dir, "module_graphs")
  dir.create(module_graphs_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  # 8.2's membership table holds each pair's kME and per-condition means.
  module_membership <- read_csv(file.path(fit_dir, "modules.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  fit_dme <- filter(dme_results, fit_id == .env$fit_id)

  for (module_name in unique(module_membership$module)) {
    module_pairs <- filter(module_membership, module == module_name)
    hub_pairs <- slice_max(module_pairs, kME, n = n_hub_pairs, with_ties = FALSE)
    hub_markers <- unique(c(hub_pairs$marker_1, hub_pairs$marker_2))
    label_markers <-
      slice_max(module_pairs, kME, n = n_label_pairs, with_ties = FALSE) |>
      with(unique(c(marker_1, marker_2)))
    # group_components() numbers components by size, largest first.
    component_markers <-
      module_pairs |>
      select(marker_1, marker_2) |>
      tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(directed = FALSE) |>
      mutate(component = tidygraph::group_components()) |>
      filter(component == 1) |>
      pull(name)
    component_pairs <- filter(module_pairs, marker_1 %in% component_markers)
    graph_nodes <-
      tibble(name = component_markers) |>
      left_join(rename(marker_categories, name = marker), by = "name") |>
      mutate(
        category = factor(replace_na(category, "unlabelled"), levels = c(names(category_palette), "unlabelled")),
        is_labelled = name %in% label_markers,
        is_hub_marker = name %in% hub_markers,
        label_face = if_else(is_hub_marker, "bold", "plain")
      )

    module_composition <-
      graph_nodes |>
      count(category) |>
      mutate(category = fct_reorder(as.character(category), n))
    composition_plot <-
      ggplot(module_composition, aes(n, category, fill = category)) +
      geom_col(colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(category_palette, unlabelled = "white"), guide = "none") +
      scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
      labs(title = paste0("Module markers (n = ", nrow(graph_nodes), ")"), x = "Markers", y = NULL)

    for (target in fit_dme$target |> unique()) {
      module_dme <- filter(fit_dme, module == module_name, target == .env$target)
      graph_edges <-
        component_pairs |>
        filter(marker_1 != marker_2) |>
        mutate(
          delta_proximity = .data[[paste0("mean_log2_ratio_", target)]] -
            .data[[paste0("mean_log2_ratio_", reference_condition)]],
          is_hub = paste(marker_1, marker_2) %in% paste(hub_pairs$marker_1, hub_pairs$marker_2)
        ) |>
        arrange(kME) # strong edges are drawn last, on top
      delta_limit <- max(abs(graph_edges$delta_proximity), 0)
      set.seed(analysis_seed)
      graph_layout <- create_layout(
        tidygraph::tbl_graph(
          nodes = graph_nodes,
          edges = rename(graph_edges, from = marker_1, to = marker_2),
          directed = FALSE
        ),
        layout = "kk"
      )

      module_graph <-
        ggraph(graph_layout) +
        geom_edge_link(aes(filter = !is_hub, colour = delta_proximity, width = kME, alpha = kME)) +
        # Hub pairs: a thin black outline under an opaque edge
        geom_edge_link(aes(filter = is_hub), colour = "black", width = 2.8) +
        geom_edge_link(aes(filter = is_hub, colour = delta_proximity), width = 2.2) +
        geom_node_point(aes(filter = !is_labelled, fill = category), shape = 21, size = 2, colour = "grey30") +
        geom_node_point(aes(filter = is_labelled & !is_hub_marker, fill = category), shape = 21, size = 2.5, colour = "grey30") +
        geom_node_point(aes(filter = is_hub_marker, fill = category), shape = 21, size = 5.5, colour = "black", stroke = 0.9) +
        # Labels are repelled so they never overlap; iterations, not time,
        # bound the search, so placement is reproducible.
        geom_node_label(
          aes(filter = is_labelled, label = name, fill = category, colour = is_hub_marker, fontface = label_face, size = is_hub_marker),
          repel = TRUE,
          max.overlaps = Inf,
          box.padding = 0.5,
          point.padding = 0.2,
          force = 8,
          force_pull = 0.5,
          max.time = 120,
          max.iter = 2e5,
          min.segment.length = 0,
          segment.colour = "grey40",
          seed = analysis_seed,
          label.size = 0.8,
          show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = hub_label_colour, `FALSE` = "grey20"), guide = "none") +
        scale_size_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 4.5, `FALSE` = 3.2), guide = "none") +
        scale_edge_colour_gradientn(colours = gradient_palette, limits = c(-1, 1) * delta_limit) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(category_palette, unlabelled = "white"), guide = "none") +
        scale_edge_width(range = c(0.1, 2.5)) +
        scale_edge_alpha(range = c(0.05, 1)) +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0.1, 0.1)) +
        scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.1, 0.1)) +
        theme(
          aspect.ratio = 1,
          panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black"),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank()
        ) +
        labs(
          x = NULL,
          y = NULL,
          edge_colour = paste0("Δ proximity\n(", target, " − ", reference_condition, ")"),
          edge_width = "Module\nmembership",
          edge_alpha = "Module\nmembership"
        )
      graph_caption <- paste0(
        "Edges: ", nrow(graph_edges), " of the module's ", nrow(module_pairs),
        " pairs (largest connected component; self-pairs not drawn) · labels: markers of the top ",
        n_label_pairs, " pairs by membership\n",
        "Hub pairs (outlined, large nodes): ",
        paste(hub_pairs$marker_1, hub_pairs$marker_2, sep = ":", collapse = ", ")
      )

      module_figure <-
        patchwork::wrap_plots(module_graph, composition_plot, widths = c(3, 1.4)) +
        patchwork::plot_annotation(
          title = paste0(
            fit_id, " · ", module_name,
            "\n", target, " vs ", reference_condition,
            ": diff_median ", signif(module_dme$diff_median, 2),
            ", adj. p ", signif(module_dme$p_adj, 2),
            if (!is.null(donor_column)) paste0(", ", module_dme$n_donors_same_direction, "/", module_dme$n_donors, " donors")
          ),
          caption = graph_caption,
          theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))
        )

      graph_file <- file.path(
        module_graphs_dir,
        if (length(target_conditions) > 1) paste0(module_name, "_", str_replace_all(target, "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_")) else module_name
      )
      # PNG through export_plot; the PDF through cairo_pdf, because the
      # default pdf() device cannot encode Δ and the minus sign.
      export_plot(filename = graph_file, plot = module_figure, width = 15, height = 8.5, file_formats = "png")
      ggsave(paste0(graph_file, ".pdf"), plot = module_figure, width = 15, height = 8.5, device = cairo_pdf)
    }
  }
}
```

## 8.5. Module preservation (opt-in)

Module preservation asks whether a network's co-proximity modules hold together in the conditions the network was not built on: the target conditions of a reference network, or the other conditions of a per-condition network. For each network and query condition, hdWGCNA's permutation test compares the network's modules with the query condition's metacells of the same stratum and cell type and summarizes the evidence as Zsummary. A Zsummary below 2 means no evidence of preservation, and above 10 means strong preservation (Langfelder 2011).

The section is skipped unless `run_preservation <- TRUE`. It is also skipped, with a warning, when `network_cells <- "all"`, because every condition then helped build the networks.

> **Decision checkpoint** (module preservation)  
> Set `run_preservation <- TRUE` to run the test. It is a permutation test per network × query condition, and its time grows with the number of metacells and with the square of the number of pairs: about 3 min at about 3k pairs, 50 metacells and 100 permutations, but about 25 min at about 3k pairs and 600–850 metacells. Lower `preservation_permutations` for a quick look; 100 is the recommended minimum.

```{r}
#| label: module08_preservation_settings

run_preservation <- FALSE
preservation_permutations <- 100
```

> **Note:** Modules of more than 1,000 marker pairs are subsampled to 1,000 pairs for the test (`maxModuleSize`), and their `module_size` in the table and plots is 1,000.

> **Note:** The results are cached under `networks/{stratum}_{cell_type}_{network}_preservation.rds`. Changing `preservation_permutations` without `rebuild_networks <- TRUE` keeps the old results.

```{r}
#| label: module08_preservation

preservation_fit_ids <- names(coproximity_fits)
if (length(coproximity_fits) == 0) {
  message("No network was fitted (see sweep_summary.csv); 8.5 is skipped.")
} else if (!run_preservation) {
  message("Module preservation skipped; set run_preservation <- TRUE to run it.")
  preservation_fit_ids <- character()
} else if (network_cells == "all") {
  warning("Module preservation skipped: with network_cells = \"all\", every condition helped build the networks.")
  preservation_fit_ids <- character()
}

preservation_results <- tibble()
for (fit_id in preservation_fit_ids) {
  fit_row <- filter(fit_index, fit_id == .env$fit_id)
  cache_path <- file.path(
    networks_dir,
    paste0(
      str_replace_all(
        paste(c(if (use_stratum_names) fit_row$stratum, fit_row$cell_type, fit_row$network), collapse = " "),
        "[^A-Za-z0-9]+",
        "_"
      ),
      "_preservation.rds"
    )
  )

  if (file.exists(cache_path) && !rebuild_networks) {
    fit_preservation <- readRDS(cache_path)
  } else {
    network_fit <- coproximity_fits[[fit_id]]
    metacell_meta <- hdWGCNA::GetMetacellObject(network_fit)[[]]
    query_conditions <- setdiff(
      intersect(all_conditions, unique(metacell_meta[[contrast_column]])),
      network_sets[[fit_row$network]]
    )
    fit_preservation <- tibble()
    # An errored test is not cached, so the next render retries it.
    preservation_failed <- FALSE

    for (query in query_conditions) {
      # The query is the query condition's metacells, read as in 8.1.
      query_object <- hdWGCNA::SetDatExpr(
        network_fit,
        group_name = query,
        group.by = contrast_column,
        assay = "proximity",
        slot = "counts",
        layer = "counts"
      )
      if (nrow(hdWGCNA::GetDatExpr(query_object)) < min_network_metacells) {
        warning(fit_id, " / ", query, ": fewer than ", min_network_metacells, " metacells; preservation skipped")
        next
      }

      preservation_result <- tryCatch(
        hdWGCNA::ModulePreservation(
          query_object,
          seurat_ref = network_fit,
          name = query,
          n_permutations = preservation_permutations,
          parallel = FALSE,
          seed = analysis_seed,
          networkType = "signed",
          corFnc = "bicor",
          savePermutedStatistics = FALSE,
          verbose = 0
        ),
        error = conditionMessage
      )
      if (is.character(preservation_result)) {
        warning(fit_id, " / ", query, ": preservation failed: ", preservation_result)
        preservation_failed <- TRUE
        next
      }

      preservation_stats <- hdWGCNA::GetModulePreservation(preservation_result, query)
      fit_preservation <- bind_rows(
        fit_preservation,
        tibble(
          fit_id = fit_id,
          query = query,
          module = rownames(preservation_stats$Z),
          module_size = preservation_stats$Z$moduleSize,
          zsummary = preservation_stats$Z$Zsummary.pres,
          median_rank = preservation_stats$obs[module, "medianRank.pres"]
        ) |>
          filter(!module %in% c("grey", "gold"))
      )
    }
    if (!preservation_failed) saveRDS(fit_preservation, cache_path)
  }

  preservation_results <- bind_rows(preservation_results, fit_preservation)
  if (nrow(fit_preservation) == 0) next

  export_plot(
    filename = file.path(fit_row$fit_dir, "preservation_zsummary"),
    plot = ggplot(fit_preservation, aes(module_size, zsummary)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = c(2, 10), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
      geom_point() +
      geom_text(aes(label = module), vjust = -0.8, size = 3) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
      facet_wrap(~query) +
      theme_bw() +
      labs(title = paste(fit_id, "module preservation"), x = "Module size (pairs)", y = "Zsummary"),
    width = 7,
    height = 4
  )
}

if (length(preservation_fit_ids) > 0) {
  write.csv(preservation_results, file.path(module08_dir, "preservation_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  preservation_results
}
```
